v: Thieves broke through walls, rammed a mall, and stole a bobsled. In Calgary.
Here are five of Calgary's strangest heists.
Number five. In twenty twenty-two, eight brass plaques honouring Victoria Cross recipients were stolen from a memorial in Currie.
The next year, plaques were taken from the Hangar Flight Museum too. The likely lure? The metal.
Number four. October twenty eighteen, northeast Calgary. Thieves broke through the walls of two businesses to reach a jewellery store.
Number three. November twenty twelve, just before four a.m. An SUV smashed into Market Mall, aiming for a jewellery store. No one was hurt.

Number two. In October twenty twenty, a bobsled shell from the movie Cool Runnings, inspired by Jamaica's team at Calgary's nineteen eighty-eight Olympics, was stolen from outside the old Ranchman's building.
Nearly two years later, police found part of it. Only part.
And number one. North Hill Shopping Centre, nineteen ninety-eight. Two men in military fatigues ambushed a Brink's cash delivery with assault rifles and tear gas.
More than eighty shots were fired. No one was hurt. And they left with nothing.
The men behind it? A former Brink's employee and a Canadian soldier. Both went to prison.
Which one is the wildest? Comment below.
